# dsh-remote
SSH remote-server operations for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).
## What dsh-remote does

`dsh-remote` lets the agent in your DSH session actually operate remote servers:
list the hosts you

already configured in `~/.ssh/config`, probe a box, run
non-interactive commands, read and edit remo

te files over SFTP, and move files
between the session workspace and a server — with a Crescent-styl

e static
command-risk review in front of every mutating action and the DSH approval
dialog as the hu

command-risk review in front of every mutating action and the DSH approval
dialog as the human gate.

It is inspired by the Crescent
operations workbench: the same idea that the agent should gather evid

ence on the
real host, one bounded action at a time, with risky commands reviewed before
execution.
## Features

- **Hosts you already have** — discovers every concrete `Host` in
`~/.ssh/config` (including `Includ

e`s) and merges a configurable host list;
the model refers to hosts by name, exactly like `ssh <name

>`.
- **Remote exec** — one-shot, non-interactive commands with working directory,
timeout, bounded

output, and a clear `[exit code: N]` result line.
- **Remote files over SFTP** — read (line-numbered

, paginated), list, write
(atomic temp + rename), exact-string edit, and upload/download transfers.

- **Persistent remote shells** — open an interactive PTY shell on a host and
keep using it across to

ol calls (`remote_shell_*`): send input, read
scrollback, interrupt with signals, close. Every submi

tted line is
risk-reviewed like `remote_exec`.
- **Live terminal mirror** — a **Remote Terminal** ta

b in the conversation's
right sidebar shows every remote command the agent runs as it runs, with
str

eamed stdout/stderr and status lines. It opens automatically on the first
command (or from the sideb
ar's Start page). See Live terminal.

- **Interactive remote terminal** — the same right-sidebar **远程终端** panel
picks an available host an

d opens DSH's native terminal attached to a
persistent, per-conversation SSH session through a local

relay: you type
commands in a real xterm, close and re-open the tab to reattach the same
session, a

nd an SSH drop reconnects automatically with backoff. See
Interactive remote terminal.
- **Quick con

nect from the host list** — one 连接 action creates the SSH
session, opens a **new conversation**, att

aches DSH's native terminal to it,
and hands the host to the agent there ("已连接远程主机 …") so operations

start
in a dedicated conversation. Failures after the switch are shown in the
远程终端 panel (never a s

ilent local shell), and 复制连接命令 copies the exact
shell line for any terminal when the native-terminal

integration is
unavailable.
- **Host manager** — add, edit and delete connection entries from the R

emote Ops
page (persisted in `$DSH_HOME/remote/hosts.json`; auth stays
environment-variable names, n

ever stored secrets).
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations

- **No persistent remote shell.** `remote_exec` is one-shot (no PTY): each call
is a fresh shell. Lo

ng-running processes must be started detached
(`nohup … &`); interactive programs (vim, top) are not

supported.
- **`remote_read` pages within `maxReadBytes`.** Line `offset`/`limit` work on
the file

window returned by one read; a file larger than `maxReadBytes`
cannot be paged past that window. Use

`remote_exec` with `tail -n`/`grep`/
`sed -n` or `remote_transfer` for very large files.
- **Worksp

ace containment is lexical.** Transfer local paths are checked
lexically against the session working

directory (no symlink resolution);
keep `allowLocalOutsideWorkspace: false` unless you need otherwi

se.
- **Saved host authentication contains references only.** The host form stores
metadata and envi

ronment-variable names, never raw passwords. Interactive
terminal connections can request a fixed pa

ssword in the masked login dialog,
retained only in Host memory; encrypted-key passphrases still use

environment
references. A restart requires entering a transient password again.
- **One connection

per host.** Operations for one host are serialized through a
single pooled SSH connection (plus Prox

yJump hops), so concurrent calls to the
same host queue rather than open many sessions.
- **No full-

screen TUI in agent shells.** `remote_shell_*` output is
line-sanitized, so `vim`/`top`/`less` are n

ot usable from the agent; use
non-interactive commands. The interactive terminal (above) is a real x

term and
supports them for the user.
- **Shell sessions and the live stream are process-local.** The

terminal mirror
retains a bounded in-memory buffer only; a harness restart clears it (the audit
tra

il persists). Interactive-terminal sessions behave the same way: the relay
keeps them across termina

l close/reload and reconnects an SSH drop, but a
harness restart starts a fresh shell on the next op

en.
- **The interactive terminal is user-driven.** It runs with the Host user's SSH
credentials and

is not gated by the agent approval policy; `allowHosts` still
restricts which hosts may be opened. T

he local bridge needs `node` on the
[该节后续省略]
## Repository privacy

Source, tests, examples, documentation and published assets must not contain
private organization na

mes, personal identifiers or real test connection details.
Use synthetic cluster/host aliases and ac

counts, reserved example domains such as
`example.test`, and documentation IP ranges (`192.0.2.0/24`

, `198.51.100.0/24`,
`203.0.113.0/24`). Keep loopback addresses for local fixture servers. Use gener

ic
paths instead of a developer's home directory.

Browser captures must disable SSH-config discovery (`includeSshConfig: false`),
use isolated fixture

inventory, and show synthetic command output rather than
local usernames or machine details. Review

images, logs, archives and package
contents before publication; never commit live connection record

, archives and package
contents before publication; never commit live connection records or secrets.
